why: Gentle circular pressure to the temporalis instantly reduces tension headaches and jaw-related temple pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Find):** Place fingertips on your temples — the hollow just behind and above the outer eye corners. **STEP 2 (Press):** Apply gentle firm circular pressure, moving in slow inward circles. **STEP 3 (Breathe):** Close eyes, breathe slowly, maintain pressure for 30-60 seconds.

why: Releasing the masseter reduces clenching, jaw fatigue, and radiating temple/cheek pain from TMJ tension.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Locate):** Clench teeth gently — feel the masseter bulge at your cheekbone. **STEP 2 (Knead):** Use 2-3 fingertips to apply slow firm circular pressure over the whole muscle. **STEP 3 (Stretch):** Open mouth as wide as comfortable, hold 5 seconds.

why: Releasing muscles at the base of the skull relieves occipital headaches and neck-origin head pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Position):** Lie on back. Make two fists and place knuckles at the base of skull where it meets the neck. **STEP 2 (Sink):** Allow head weight to sink slowly onto knuckles for 1-2 minutes. **STEP 3 (Roll):** Gently roll head side to side 3-4 times.

why: Manually relaxing the frontalis muscle breaks the tension-headache cycle caused by sustained frowning or screen time.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Start):** Place fingertips flat across your forehead. **STEP 2 (Smooth):** Applying light pressure, drag fingers upward toward hairline, then separate sideways to temples. **STEP 3 (Repeat):** Work from centre outward in overlapping strokes.
process: 2 minutes of slow strokes. Combine with slow nasal breathing.

common_name: neck head drop chin chest cervic
why: Slow gravity-assisted head drops decompress the cervical spine and quieten headache signals at the skull base.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit tall):** Sit in a chair with spine erect. **STEP 2 (Drop):** Let chin fall gently toward chest. Hold 20 seconds. **STEP 3 (Side):** Roll right ear toward right shoulder. Hold 20 seconds. Mirror on left.
process: 3 rounds each direction. Move very slowly — no bouncing.

common_name: chin tuck neck head cervic posture
why: Corrects forward-head posture which compresses the skull base and is the number-one cause of chronic tension headaches.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Wall):** Stand with back against a wall. **STEP 2 (Tuck):** Draw chin straight back (not down) until back of head touches wall. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 5 seconds, release, repeat.
process: 10 reps x 3 sets. Do this every hour at a desk.

why: Lengthens the left SCM and scalene muscles to relieve one-sided neck stiffness and nerve compression.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit upright, feet flat. **STEP 2 (Tilt):** Tilt right ear toward right shoulder until strong pull on left neck. **STEP 3 (Deepen):** Place right hand gently on left temple for added pressure. Hold 30 seconds.
process: 3 holds x 30 seconds. Switch sides if needed.

why: Targets the right SCM and scalene muscles to relieve right-sided neck tightness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit upright, feet flat. **STEP 2 (Tilt):** Tilt left ear toward left shoulder until pull on right neck. **STEP 3 (Deepen):** Place left hand gently on right temple. Hold 30 seconds.

why: Stretches posterior cervical extensor muscles and sub-occipital group to relieve back-of-neck tightness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit upright. **STEP 2 (Lower):** Slowly bring chin toward chest until stretch at back of neck. **STEP 3 (Deepen):** Clasp hands behind head and let weight add gentle pressure. Hold 30-45 seconds.

common_name: scalene anterior neck stretch front cervic
why: Opens the front of the neck to relieve tightness from prolonged looking down and reduces brachial plexus pressure.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit tall, place right hand on collarbone to hold skin down. **STEP 2 (Tilt):** Tilt head back and to right, looking at ceiling. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel stretch along front-left of neck. Hold 30 seconds, switch.

why: Targets the muscle running from C1-C4 to shoulder blade — a primary source of stiff neck pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Anchor):** Sit and tuck right hand under sitting bone to anchor shoulder. **STEP 2 (Rotate):** Turn head 45 degrees to left. **STEP 3 (Lower):** Drop chin toward left armpit until stretch at base of right neck. Hold 30 seconds.

why: Slowly mobilises all cervical joints to increase synovial fluid and prepare the neck for activity.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Start):** Sit or stand tall. **STEP 2 (Roll):** Let head drop gently to right, roll forward to chest, then to left, back to upright. Do NOT go full backward. **STEP 3 (Reverse):** Repeat in opposite direction.
process: 5 slow circles each direction. Take 10 seconds per circle.

why: Builds deep cervical flexor endurance to reduce chronic neck fatigue and prevent repeat injury.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Hand):** Place palm flat on right temple. **STEP 2 (Press):** Push head into hand while hand resists — no movement. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Maintain tension for 10 seconds. Repeat on all four sides.
process: 10 sec x 5 reps per direction. Build to 15 seconds.

common_name: chin tuck wall neck cervic posture alignment
why: Retrains the deep neck flexors and counters forward-head posture which causes chronic neck pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Wall):** Stand with back, shoulders, and head against wall. **STEP 2 (Tuck):** Without lifting chin, pull head straight back until it lightly touches wall. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 5 seconds, relax forward, repeat.
process: 15 reps x 2 sets per hour at a screen.

why: A restorative pose allowing complete passive lengthening of all neck muscles using only gravity.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit cross-legged on floor. **STEP 2 (Drop):** Let right ear fall toward right shoulder. **STEP 3 (Arms):** Let both arms rest heavily in lap to anchor shoulders down. Breathe and hold 1 minute per side.

common_name: trapezius upper trap cross body shoulder stretch
why: Directly stretches the upper trapezius belly to release the knot of tightness between neck and shoulder.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Anchor):** Sit and hold seat edge with right hand to anchor that shoulder. **STEP 2 (Tilt):** Place left hand on head and gently pull left ear toward left shoulder. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel pull along top of right shoulder. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: levator scapulae shoulder base neck trapezius
why: Releases levator scapulae at the shoulder blade attachment — a hotspot for chronic tension.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Find):** Reach right hand over left shoulder, press fingertips into muscle where neck meets shoulder. **STEP 2 (Press):** Apply firm pressure and hold. **STEP 3 (Move):** Gently turn head away from the side you are pressing. Hold 30 seconds.
process: 2-3 minutes per side working into tight spots.

why: Lengthens the left upper trapezius fibers to restore shoulder elevation symmetry.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Anchor):** Sit and anchor left hand under thigh. **STEP 2 (Tilt):** Tilt right ear to right shoulder and look slightly down. **STEP 3 (Breathe):** Relax left shoulder away from ear. Hold 30-45 seconds.

why: Lengthens the right upper trapezius to relieve unilateral shoulder elevation and tension.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Anchor):** Sit and anchor right hand under thigh. **STEP 2 (Tilt):** Tilt left ear to left shoulder and look slightly down. **STEP 3 (Breathe):** Relax right shoulder away from ear. Hold 30-45 seconds.

why: Contracts then fully releases the trapezius, flushing stagnant fluid and warming tissue before activity.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lift):** Inhale and shrug both shoulders up toward ears as high as possible. **STEP 2 (Hold):** Hold at top for 2 seconds. **STEP 3 (Drop):** Exhale forcefully and let shoulders crash down — feel the release.

why: Passively rotates the thoracic spine and opens the traps/rhomboids in a restorative position.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Tabletop):** Start on hands and knees. **STEP 2 (Thread):** Slide right arm under body to left, lowering right shoulder and ear to mat. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Keep left arm extended or press into floor. Hold 1 minute per side.

why: Strengthens the lower trapezius and rotator cuff — muscles that counterbalance chronic upper trap overload.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Prone):** Lie face down, arms at sides. **STEP 2 (Y):** Lift arms diagonally in a Y shape, thumbs up. Hold 2 seconds. **STEP 3 (T then W):** Bring arms to a T, then bend elbows into a W, squeezing shoulder blades. Lower slowly.

why: Retrains scapular upward rotation and lower trap activation to counteract rounded-shoulder posture.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Wall):** Stand with back flat against wall, feet 3cm away. Press low back, upper back, and head into wall. **STEP 2 (Arms):** Raise arms into goalpost (90 degrees) against wall. **STEP 3 (Slide):** Slowly slide arms overhead, keeping all contact. Slide back down.

why: Opens the left pectoralis major to relieve anterior chest tightness and reduce compression on left-side ribs.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Doorway):** Stand in doorframe, place left forearm against it at 90 degrees. **STEP 2 (Step):** Step right foot forward, rotating chest to right. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel stretch across left chest. Hold 30 seconds.

why: Opens the right pectoralis major to relieve right anterior chest tightness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Doorway):** Stand in doorframe, place right forearm against it at 90 degrees. **STEP 2 (Step):** Step left foot forward, rotating chest to left. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel stretch across right chest. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: pectoralis sternum chest cross body stretch
why: Relieves costal and sternal tightness by externally rotating both arms and expanding the ribcage.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand tall, feet shoulder-width. **STEP 2 (Clasp):** Clasp hands behind lower back. **STEP 3 (Open):** Squeeze shoulder blades together, lift chest, gently roll fists downward. Hold 20-30 seconds.

common_name: pec minor collarbone chest stretch clavicle
why: Stretches pec minor near the coracoid process to relieve collarbone pressure and subclavian tension.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Corner):** Stand in corner with both hands on walls. **STEP 2 (Press):** Lean body forward, keeping elbows below shoulder height. **STEP 3 (Focus):** Concentrate stretch high on chest just below collarbones. Hold 30 seconds.

why: Gently extends the thoracic spine backward and opens the entire anterior chest and anterior shoulders.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Prone):** Lie face down, hands under shoulders, elbows close to body. **STEP 2 (Press):** Inhale and slowly press chest off floor, straightening arms to comfortable limit. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Draw shoulder blades down and back. Hold 20-30 seconds.

why: Dynamically warms up pec fibers, anterior deltoids, and shoulder capsule before upper-body activity.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Cross):** Cross both arms in front of chest. **STEP 2 (Swing):** Swing them out wide to sides like wings, squeezing shoulder blades. **STEP 3 (Alternate):** Swing back to cross, alternating which arm is on top.

why: Strengthens the pectorals, anterior deltoid, and triceps — building the anterior chain that supports the chest wall.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Plank):** Start in high plank — hands under shoulders, body straight. **STEP 2 (Lower):** Bend elbows to 45 degrees and lower chest to 3cm from floor. **STEP 3 (Press):** Push back up fully, squeezing chest at top.
process: 10-15 reps, 3 sets. Knees down if needed.

why: Reverses the hunched posture that chronically shortens the chest by passively extending the thoracic spine.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Chair):** Sit in hard chair, place rolled towel along upper back. **STEP 2 (Arch):** Support head with hands and lean back over towel. **STEP 3 (Breathe):** Let gravity open chest. Hold 20-30 seconds.

why: Stretches the left rhomboid and middle trapezius to relieve the aching knot between spine and shoulder blade.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Cross):** Reach left arm across body at shoulder height. **STEP 2 (Hook):** Use right hand to pull left elbow closer to chest. **STEP 3 (Round):** Round upper back and feel stretch at left inner shoulder blade. Hold 30 seconds.

why: Stretches the right rhomboid and middle trapezius to release the knot between spine and right blade.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Cross):** Reach right arm across body at shoulder height. **STEP 2 (Hook):** Use left hand to pull right elbow closer to chest. **STEP 3 (Round):** Round upper back and feel stretch at right inner blade. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: thoracic cat cow upper back between blades
why: Alternately shortens and lengthens mid-back muscles to release chronic tension between shoulder blades.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Tabletop):** On hands and knees. **STEP 2 (Cat):** Push through hands, rounding entire upper back toward ceiling — feel blades separate. **STEP 3 (Cow):** Inhale, let upper back drop and spine arch between blades.
process: 10-15 slow cycles. Focus awareness between shoulder blades.

why: Mobilises thoracic vertebral joints that become locked from prolonged sitting, causing mid-back stiffness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit sideways on a chair, feet flat. **STEP 2 (Hands):** Cross arms over chest. **STEP 3 (Rotate):** Rotate torso toward chair back, using it as a gentle end-range stop. Hold 10 seconds. Repeat other side.

common_name: thread needle thoracic rhomboid blade yoga
why: Passively rotates thoracic spine left, releasing the right rhomboid and left serratus anterior.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Tabletop):** Start on hands and knees. **STEP 2 (Thread):** Slide right arm under body to left, lowering right shoulder to mat. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Extend left arm forward for balance. Hold 1 minute.

common_name: rhomboid row band upper back squeeze
why: Strengthens rhomboids, middle trapezius, and rear deltoids — muscles that prevent forward-shoulder collapse.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Band):** Stand on resistance band, holding one end in each hand. **STEP 2 (Hinge):** Hinge 30 degrees forward at hips. **STEP 3 (Row):** Pull band up to lower ribs, elbows back, squeezing shoulder blades together. Lower slowly.

common_name: thoracic wall slide posture upper back rhomboid
why: Trains the mid-back to hold an upright position against the wall, correcting the forward hunch at root cause.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Wall):** Stand with spine flat against wall. **STEP 2 (Arms):** Place arms in goalpost shape touching wall. **STEP 3 (Slide):** Slowly slide arms overhead, keeping entire back in contact. Slide back down.

why: Lengthens biceps brachii to relieve anterior elbow and shoulder tightness from repeated curling motions.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Wall):** Stand facing wall, place right palm flat on it at shoulder height, thumb up. **STEP 2 (Rotate):** Rotate body away from wall, keeping palm in contact. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel pull from shoulder to elbow. Hold 30 seconds.

why: Stretches long head of triceps from scapula to elbow, relieving posterior arm and elbow pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lift):** Raise right arm, bend elbow, let right hand fall behind head. **STEP 2 (Assist):** Use left hand to gently push right elbow further behind head. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel pull from armpit down back of arm. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: deltoid cross body shoulder arm stretch
why: Targets posterior deltoid and capsule — relieves the deep ache at back of shoulder following overhead work.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Cross):** Bring right arm straight across chest. **STEP 2 (Hook):** Use left forearm to hold and pull right arm closer to chest. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel pull at back of right shoulder. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: elbow brachialis arm stretch tennis elbow
why: Reduces tightness in brachialis and bicep tendon at elbow crease, relieving elbow flexion stiffness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Extend):** Straighten arm fully. **STEP 2 (Supinate):** Rotate forearm so palm faces upward. **STEP 3 (Mild pull):** Use other hand to gently press wrist further back. Hold 20-30 seconds.

why: Lubricates the shoulder joint, warms biceps and deltoid, and increases blood flow before lifting.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Small):** Extend arms sideways, make 10 small forward circles. **STEP 2 (Large):** Increase to large sweeping circles, 10 reps. **STEP 3 (Reverse):** Repeat both sizes backward.

common_name: cow face pose tricep deltoid arm yoga
why: Provides a deep simultaneous stretch for one tricep and one shoulder, restoring full overhead range.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Right up):** Raise right arm, bend elbow, hand behind head. **STEP 2 (Left behind):** Bring left arm behind back and try to clasp fingers. **STEP 3 (Hold):** If unable to clasp, hold a towel between hands. Hold 45 seconds.

common_name: isometric bicep hold arm brachii wall
why: Builds bicep tensile strength without joint movement — safe for acute elbow or shoulder pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Position):** Stand in doorway, place forearm under frame at 90 degrees. **STEP 2 (Press):** Push forearm up into frame as hard as possible. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Maintain maximum effort for 10 seconds.

common_name: external rotation cuff deltoid arm shoulder posture
why: Strengthens external rotators to undo the internal rotation pattern causing shoulder impingement and bicep pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Elbow):** Stand with elbow bent 90 degrees at side, holding light resistance band. **STEP 2 (Rotate):** Keeping elbow glued to side, rotate forearm outward. **STEP 3 (Control):** Return slowly — focus on back of shoulder.

common_name: wrist flexor stretch forearm prayer inner
why: Lengthens wrist flexors along the inner forearm to relieve Golfer's elbow and carpal tunnel pressure.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Prayer):** Bring both palms together in prayer position. **STEP 2 (Lower):** Slowly lower hands toward waist, keeping palms pressed together. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel pull along inner forearms. Hold 30 seconds.

why: Stretches the extensor muscle along the outer forearm to relieve Tennis elbow pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Extend):** Extend right arm forward, palm facing you. **STEP 2 (Flex):** Use left hand to gently pull right fingers and wrist toward body. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel pull along outer forearm. Hold 30 seconds.

why: Specifically stretches the brachioradialis — the primary driver of lateral elbow pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Arm out):** Hold right arm straight in front, palm down. **STEP 2 (Curl wrist):** Bend right wrist downward. **STEP 3 (Pull):** Use left hand to add gentle downward pressure on right fingers. Hold 20 seconds.

common_name: golfers elbow medial inner forearm stretch
why: Targets the flexor-pronator mass at the medial epicondyle — the cause of Golfer's elbow pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Extend):** Straighten right arm in front, palm up. **STEP 2 (Cock back):** Use left hand to bend right wrist back (fingers up). **STEP 3 (Pronate):** Slightly internally rotate arm while maintaining stretch. Hold 30 seconds.

why: Lubricates the wrist and distal radioulnar joints and warms forearm muscles before gripping.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Fist):** Make loose fists. **STEP 2 (Circle):** Slowly rotate both wrists in large circles — 10 reps clockwise. **STEP 3 (Reverse):** 10 reps counter-clockwise.

why: Strengthens the wrist flexors for balanced forearm strength and reduced repetitive strain injury risk.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit and rest forearm on thigh, palm up, holding light weight. **STEP 2 (Lower):** Lower weight toward floor. **STEP 3 (Curl):** Curl wrist up as far as it will go. Lower slowly.

common_name: reverse wrist curl forearm extensor outer
why: Strengthens the extensor group to correct the flexor/extensor imbalance causing Tennis elbow.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Rest forearm on thigh, palm facing down. **STEP 2 (Lower):** Let weight dangle. **STEP 3 (Lift):** Raise back of hand toward ceiling. Lower slowly.

why: Corrects the flexed-wrist typing posture that progressively tightens the forearm and strains the carpal tunnel.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Desk):** Ensure wrists are straight at desk — not bent up or down. **STEP 2 (Shake):** Shake out wrists for 10 seconds to reset blood flow. **STEP 3 (Reset):** Place forearms on desk surface so wrists are fully supported and neutral.
process: Check wrist position every 30 minutes. Do shake-out hourly.

why: Moves the flexor tendons through their full range inside the carpal tunnel, reducing finger pain and stiffness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Straight):** Hold hand out, fingers straight. **STEP 2 (Tabletop):** Bend fingers at large knuckles only — like a tabletop — keeping tips straight. Hold 3 seconds. **STEP 3 (Fist):** Curl into a full gentle fist. Hold 3 seconds. Straighten and repeat.

why: Restores full range of the thumb CMC joint and relieves the ache at the base of the thumb from de Quervain's or overuse.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Ready):** Hold hand open. **STEP 2 (Touch):** Bring tip of thumb to touch tip of little finger. **STEP 3 (Sequence):** Move back through each finger — ring, middle, index. Repeat both directions.

why: Opens the intrinsic muscles of the palm and palmar fascia — relieves palm cramping and tightness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Press):** Interlace fingers of both hands. **STEP 2 (Flip):** Turn palms outward away from you and straighten elbows. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel the deep stretch through both palms. Hold 20-30 seconds.

common_name: wrist ulnar radial deviation hand stretch carpal
why: Mobilises the radiocarpal joint and stretches ulnar and radial ligaments compressed by sustained gripping.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Extend):** Extend right arm forward, palm down. **STEP 2 (Ulnar):** Bend wrist toward ground (ulnar deviation). Hold 10 seconds. **STEP 3 (Radial):** Bend wrist back toward thumb (radial deviation). Hold 10 seconds.

why: Opens the ulnar side of the hand and stretches hypothenar muscles causing pinky-side aching.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Spread):** Place hand palm-up on flat surface. **STEP 2 (Pull):** Use other hand to gently pull little finger away from ring finger. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold the gentle separation for 15 seconds.

why: Individually stretches the flexor digitorum tendon of the ring finger — the most commonly adhered tendon in trigger finger.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Isolate):** Hold all other fingers bent and curl only ring finger into palm. **STEP 2 (Extend):** Use opposite thumb to gently extend just the ring finger. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 15 seconds, feel the dorsal pull.

common_name: hand shake wrist finger warmup grip
why: Rapidly increases blood flow to intrinsic hand muscles and wrist joints before fine motor activities.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Dangle):** Let both arms hang loosely at sides. **STEP 2 (Shake):** Rapidly shake hands from wrists as if flicking water. **STEP 3 (Up):** Raise arms overhead and shake briefly, then circle back down.

common_name: grip squeeze hand strength finger metacarpal
why: Builds balanced gripping strength to reduce fatigue-related finger and wrist pain during repetitive tasks.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Ball):** Hold soft stress ball or rolled towel. **STEP 2 (Squeeze):** Squeeze as hard as comfortably possible. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 5 seconds, fully relax 5 seconds.

common_name: neutral hand wrist ergonomic posture carpal
why: Teaching the hand to rest in a neutral cup shape prevents hyperextension and overgripping that strains tendons.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Cup):** Let hand rest in a natural cup shape — not flat, not clenched. **STEP 2 (Check):** Fingers should be gently curved, wrist straight. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Maintain this shape for a minute as the default resting position.
process: Practice for 2 minutes, 3-4 times per day at a desk.
